body.heading: Where in the world is Malta?
paragraphs: Malta is a country in Southern Europe, which is part of Europe. It is an island country, surrounded by sea.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Malta is Valletta.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: People in Malta speak Maltese and English.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Malta is the euro. The euro is shared by many countries in Europe, so the same coins and notes work across borders.

body.heading: How big is Malta?
paragraphs: Malta covers about 316 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about twice the size of Liechtenstein.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Valletta is a golden-stone fortress capital built by knights, with St John's Co-Cathedral glittering inside, harbour cannons and grand harbour boat tours.
Between Malta and Gozo, Comino's Blue Lagoon is a pool of impossible turquoise over white sand — the country's favourite swimming spot.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Malta on a map or globe. Which continent is it nearest to — and what sea or ocean surrounds it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?

takeaway: Malta in one breath: a country in Southern Europe, capital Valletta, where people speak Maltese and pay with the euro.
